proof.claim:
The two doctor surfaces must not contradict each other. A cluster-scoped
finding shown on a node's page must be one the cluster report actually holds.

WHY THIS EXISTS. On 2026-08-19 globular-admin showed "Worst Severity:
CRITICAL" on all five nodes of a completely healthy cluster. The finding was
objectstore.write_quorum_lost — "active_drives=1 < write_quorum=3" — against
a MinIO pool that was, at that moment, 4 drives online / 0 offline / EC:2,
with an object written on one node and read back byte-identical from all
four.

The tell was that the finding named a DIFFERENT sole survivor on every page:

  viewing globule-ryzen   -> active_nodes=10.0.0.63,  down=[.102 .9 .8]
  viewing globule-nuc     -> active_nodes=10.0.0.8,   down=[.63 .102 .9]
  viewing globule-hp-01   -> active_nodes=10.0.0.9,   down=[.63 .102 .8]
  viewing globule-lenovo  -> active_nodes=10.0.0.102, down=[.63 .9 .8]

All four cannot each be the last one standing. known_down_nodes was empty in
every case: nothing had ever been observed down.

THE CAUSE. EvaluateForNode builds a snapshot whose Nodes list is filtered to
the single node being reported on, then evaluates CLUSTER-scoped rules
against that view. Rules that resolve membership see every other node as
absent — no NodeRecord, no inventory — and count them down. The verdict was
assembled entirely from nodes missing from a deliberately narrowed snapshot,
which is the shape ops.always.doctor.reduced-harvest-honesty exists to
forbid: a reduced harvest is an UNKNOWN, never a FAIL.

WHY THE CLUSTER REPORT ALONE CANNOT CATCH IT. `globular doctor report
cluster` was clean throughout — it is the only surface that receives the full
node set. doctor-report-clean asks exactly that surface and would have passed
on every one of those days while every node page showed CRITICAL. The
divergence between the surfaces is the defect, so the divergence is what this
asserts.

DIRECTIONALITY. Only findings present in the NODE report and absent from the
CLUSTER report fail this scenario. The reverse is legitimate — the cluster
report may hold cluster-scoped findings a node page does not surface — and is
recorded but never failed on.

WHY ALL FIVE NODES. The defect was per-node by construction: each page
indicted the other four. Checking one node would catch it here, but checking
every node is what distinguishes "this surface is broken" from "this one node
is odd", and it costs one probe each.

NOT COVERED HERE: whether either report is CORRECT about the cluster. This
pins agreement, not truth. A doctor that is wrong in the same way on both
surfaces passes this scenario and is caught by doctor-report-clean and by the
objectstore scenarios.
